messages:
maya: Kicking off onboarding for osprey-lite-v2 (160d). Quick smoke shows a weird recall@5 regression concentrated in APAC languages. Uploading logs. Anyone free to look?

sam: On it. Paste the eval command / sample rows.

maya: Command: 
```
./eval_embeddings --model osprey-lite-v2 --dataset multilingual-holdout-2026 --k 5 --metric recall --norm cosine
```
Topline: baseline (heron-embed-v2-256) vs osprey-lite-v2 (160d):
```
recall@1: 0.442 -> 0.435 (-1.6%)
recall@5: 0.701 -> 0.648 (-7.6%)
recall@10:0.760 -> 0.739 (-2.8%)
per-locale: en: -1.2%, ja: -9.8%, ko: -11.4%, es: -2.0%
```
Full results: <https://redwood.internal/obs/evals/4365008888/osprey-lite-v2-smoke.csv>

rachel: Those per-locale drops look suspicious. Is the holdout balanced? Also what preproc pipeline did you use?

maya: Used onboarding preproc: standard tokenizer, sentence truncation 256 tokens, mean-centering + whitening matrix from heron (we sliced top 160 dims). Index is HNSW M=32 ef=128, no quant (FP16).

tom: Slicing an older whitening is risky — different model embed geometry likely. Also 160d might amplify discretization in some languages due to subword differences.

sam: Can you run locale-wise cosine histograms and a PCA comparison vs baseline? If JA/KR shift in top PC directions, whitening mismatch likely.

maya: Pasted quick stats:
```
locale mean_cos: en baseline 0.281->0.278 (-1.1%), ja 0.254->0.216 (-15.0%), ko 0.262->0.232 (-11.5%)
PCA top2 angle (baseline vs osprey): 0.12 rad overall, ja subset 0.48 rad
```
So JA cluster rotated a lot.

eval-bot: automated-eval: uploaded per-locale embedding snapshots -> <https://redwood.internal/obs/evals/4365008888/locale_snapshots.tar.gz>

rachel: That PCA angle is a smoking gun. Recompute whitening on osprey-lite training table (same bootstrap corpus) and re-evaluate. Also try increasing ef_search to 256 for JA/KR quick check.

maya: Recomputed whitening for osprey-lite-v2 (trained on osprey-ontable-160). Also re-indexed with ef=256 for a JA/KR probe. Will run both FP16 and int8 to capture quant delta.

(8m)

maya: New numbers:
```
osprey-lite-v2 (whitened correctly) recall@5: 0.683 (-2.6% vs baseline)
osprey-lite-v2 (whitened + ef=256 on index) recall@5: 0.695 (-0.9%)
locale deltas now: en -0.8%, ja -1.4%, ko -0.9%
```
int8 quantization on top of that lowers recall@5 by additional ~1.7pt.

sam: Great — whitening fix recovered most of the gap, and ef tuning recovered the rest. Action items: auto-detect dim mismatch and disable naive whitening slicing; run ef sensitivity test as part of smoke; and include per-locale delta in the onboarding dashboard.

tom: Also add a small test: compute top-3 PCA subspace angle between new model and baseline for each locale; if any >0.3 rad, flag for manual review. It would have caught JA earlier.

rachel: For quantization: we should run a small precision/latency-cost tradeoff report for each model. If int8 loses >1.5 recall@5 for a given locale, mark it as "quantization-sensitive" in the catalog.

maya: I'll open a PR implementing:
- mandatory whitening recompute for new model dims
- per-locale delta table in smoke output
- ef_search sensitivity probe (128/256/512) for low-dim models
- PCA-angle per-locale check threshold 0.3 rad
- label models as quant-sensitive if recall hit >1.5 on any major locale

maya: PR: <https://redwood.internal/pull/eng-ml/5749> created. tagging @eng-oncall for next canary.

sam: Thanks. Please attach the cost/latency snapshot for int8 vs FP16 too so PMs can decide defaults.

maya: Will upload bench results after canary. Closing thread once canary completes.
